agent.result_text:
Done. I wrote the acceptance test and verified it against the running app.

## What I did

**New spec: `e2e/specs/invoice-notes.spec.ts`** — four tests covering the change request *"Let me add notes to invoices too. Not just jobs."*, modelled on the existing `project-notes.spec.ts`:

1. **Empty state** — an invoice with no notes of its own shows `invoice-notes-empty`, not `invoice-notes-list`; a note on a *different* invoice doesn't leak in.
2. **Own notes, newest first** — three notes on invoice 1 render keyed by id (`note-row-<id>` / `note-text`) in `at`-descending order (deliberately unrelated to id/insertion order), while a note on another invoice and a note on a *project* (same id-space, different target type) are excluded.
3. **Writing a note** — via the shared `note-form` lands at the top of the list and survives a reload.
4. **First note on an empty invoice** replaces the empty state with the list.

All assert only through the UI (`data-testid`) and the audit file, which stays empty throughout (notes aren't audited). It uses the 3 new anchors (`invoice-notes`, `invoice-notes-empty`, `invoice-notes-list`) plus the shared `note-*` anchors.

**No existing tests needed updating** — only `project-notes` uses the shared `note-*` anchors and it stays scoped to projects; the change is purely additive.

## Verification

- All 4 new tests **fail for the right reason** against the current app: `invoice-detail-page` renders (so navigation + seeding work), but the not-yet-built `invoice-notes` region is absent.
- I confirmed the existing `project-notes` spec's behaviour to validate a subtle seeding decision.

## One finding worth flagging

While validating, I found the app matches note `targetType` with a **case-sensitive** SQL equality, and the shipped front-end queries/writes **lowercase** (`targetType=project`). The existing `project-notes.spec.ts` seeds uppercase `'PROJECT'`, so **2 of its tests are already failing** (the seeded-display ones) independent of my change. To avoid the same trap, my spec seeds lowercase `'invoice'`/`'project'` so the display tests will pass against a correct implementation (which will mirror the project feature's lowercase query). I recorded this gotcha in memory. I did not touch `project-notes.spec.ts`, since this change request doesn't revise project-notes behaviour.
